def: The set of tools, formats and feedback through which a language model operates a system, designed with the care a human interface gets.
Giving related tools a shared prefix, such as billing_ or crm_, so a model can tell tools from different systems apart as the list grows.
The prose in a tool definition that tells the model what the tool does, when to use it, what its arguments mean and what it does not return.
Mistake-proofing: designing an interface, for example with enums and bounded types, so that the wrong call is hard or impossible to write.
A tool parameter, such as a concise or detailed enum, that lets the agent choose how much detail a result contains.
Cutting an oversized tool result and telling the model that it was cut and how to narrow the next request.
A tool error that says what went wrong, what is valid and whether anything changed, so the model's next call can be a fix and not a repeat.
A caller-chosen token sent with a write so that repeating the request has the same effect as sending it once.
A tool mode that reports what the action would do without changing anything.
A script that checks tool definitions for known weaknesses such as thin descriptions, generic argument names and overlapping tools.
